claim_one_line: THE COMMON POINT IN TARGETS OF HIGHER RANK (sealed 8b91162f8 before the run; output bb43604dd committed unread; every cell holds): in every target tested -- SU(2), U(3), U(5), finite irreducible images -- a common point of the weave of n records exists only at n = 2, and at n = 2 the targets that have one are exactly the Heisenberg groups (Q8, the p = 2 Pauli group; H(3); H(5)), every generating pair fixed by every move; 2T, A4, S4, A5, Delta(54) and PSL(2,7) have none even at n = 2; at n = 3 H(3)'s 3 888 filtered triples are all moved; at n = 4 none. The common point of two records is a commutator-pairing (Heisenberg) point, the moves preserving the pairing exactly in rank two (SL(2) = Sp(2)); a target supplies only the prime p. p = 2 gives the quaternion point and its three parity directions (the triplet, T2); p = 3 gives a 3-dimensional point whose 8 directions are not a triplet. 0 of 19.
